title: Staged tenant warmup and gentle evacuation scheduler
author: Maya Owens
release_notes: Introduce a staged tenant warmup path and a gentle evacuation scheduler to reduce oscillatory evictions during regional disturbances; adds telemetry and feature-flagged rollout.
body:
Context and motivation:
Incidents over the last quarter (see ENG-7821) showed repeated oscillation where tenants that were briefly removed by the SLO enforcer re-entered traffic too aggressively and triggered cascading evictions. This led to repeated regional failovers and increased latency for steady-state tenants. The existing eviction policy is binary (evict / reinstate) and does not account for a gradual re-admission profile or a coordinated, staggered drain when capacity is constrained.

This PR implements two coordinated capabilities: (1) staged tenant warmup: when a tenant is reinstated after being shelved or moved, we gradually ramp its allowed admission rate over a configurable warmup window; and (2) gentle evacuation scheduler: when performing tenant evacuation (manual or automatic due to node/region pressure), we schedule staggered drain windows with small reservation slices for higher-priority tenants to avoid mass reconnect storms.

High-level changes (single-line summary):
- Add warmup state machine and admission token bucket per-tenant with decay schedules.
- Introduce evacuation scheduler that computes per-tenant drain windows and emits soft-deny decisions rather than immediate hard evictions.
- Tie warmup and scheduler into the SLO enforcer and circuit-breaker signals so tenants marked unhealthy take a slower path to rejoining.
- New telemetry: tenant_warmup_progress, evacuation_window_start, staged_evacuations_active, warmup_penalty_decay_seconds.
- Added feature flag (runtime with default OFF) and config knobs: warmup_window_seconds, step_increment_pct, reservation_slices, max_stagger_seconds.

Implementation notes:
The warmup implementation is in runtime/admission and uses the same admission-token framework as prior soft-doors but layered with a per-tenant timer and exponential decay on penalty ledger entries. Warmup applies only after a tenant exits a shelved or quarantined state; tenants that were preempted for SLA violations still go through the same process but with an initial lower admission cap. The evacuation scheduler is a lightweight orchestrator in controlplane/evac that receives the ordered list of tenants to drain and computes soft windows; it returns admit/soft-deny hints to the fronting admission layer so we can maintain short-circuit low-latency decisions at request time.

Compatibility and migration:
- Backwards compatible: when the feature flag is off, behavior is unchanged.
- Default values are conservative (warmup_window_seconds=120, step_increment_pct=20, reservation_slices=3, max_stagger_seconds=90) to ensure safe behavior in canaries.
- No database schema changes; state is kept in existing ephemeral tenant-lease store with a small additional key namespace.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests cover warmup state transitions, token refill math, and scheduler slot allocation.
- Integration test harness simulates a regional node drain and confirms staged rejoin avoids >30% oscillation compared to baseline.
- Added a small load canary on staging with 5% traffic for 24h before prod rollout.

Rollout plan:
- Feature flag default OFF in main.
- Canary in region-us-west-2 at 5% traffic for 24h (observability checklist attached).
- Gradual ramp to 25% then 50% if no anomalies in SLO delta, otherwise automatic rollback.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Integration tests added
- [x] Telemetry events instrumented
- [x] Feature-flag gating and default-off config
- [x] Docs stub for runtime knobs and runbook updates

Related work and references:
- ENG-7821: incident writeup on oscillatory evictions
- SUP-4392: customer impact report (tenant X)

Notes to reviewers:
- The warmup math is intentionally conservative; if we want more aggressive re-admit we can expose step_increment_pct as a per-tenant override in a follow-up.
- The scheduler uses a best-effort time wheel; it's non-blocking and tolerates controller restarts by consulting the tenant-lease store.

Merge rationale:
Fixes a high-severity class of customer-visible instability and is behind a feature flag so we can iterate safely. The change is small enough to be rolled back quickly if needed.
commits: c1f8b2f: introduce warmup state machine and token-bucket logic
d4a9e03: add evacuation scheduler and orchestration hooks in controlplane/evac
e7b2c44: telemetry metrics and alert rules for staged evacuations
f3c6a11: unit/integration tests + feature flag configuration
review_comments: Diego Morales: Can we make sure the warmup token refill uses a monotonic clock? There were subtle flakes in CI related to time.Now() vs monotonic. (requested change)
Maya Owens: Good catch — switched to runtime/clock package in the latest commit and added deterministic clock for tests. (reply)
Priya Singh: I want to see the canary dashboard panels for the new metrics before merging. Please add a link to the staging Grafana snapshot. (request)
Maya Owens: Grafana snapshot link added to observability/metrics/metrics.yaml and docs/runbooks/evacuation.md includes expected thresholds. (reply)
Ethan Burke: lgtm for runtime side; noted one minor naming nit in scheduler_test.go which I left inline. (approved)
testing_plan: Canary in us-west-2 at 5% for 24h with SLO delta and eviction-oscillation panels. If SLO delta > 2% or oscillation metric > baseline*0.7, rollback the feature flag. Run a targeted tenant probe for heavy tenants after 6h.
notes: This is a targeted reliability improvement focused on tenant admission and evacuation flow. No customer-facing API changes. Operational runbook added to docs/runbooks/evacuation.md.
